detail.body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Scope: this is a kernel-level microbenchmark, not an end-to-end throughput claim.**
> The numbers below are measured on the isolated kernel, both versions in the same process. Against a multi-millisecond decode step a
> change of this size sits inside run-to-run variation (~1% on a conc=1 arm), so
> **no measurable serving throughput improvement is claimed, and none should be
> inferred.** The value is removing six of seven kernel launches on a path that is
> on the critical path at low concurrency.

## Purpose

`mamba_get_block_table_tensor`'s `"align"` branch takes the last `1 + num_speculative_blocks` block-table entries of each request:

```python
start_indices = (seq_lens - 1) // kv_cache_spec.block_size
start_indices.clamp_(min=0)
offsets = torch.arange(1 + kv_cache_spec.num_speculative_blocks, ...)
indices_to_gather = (start_indices.unsqueeze(1) + offsets).to(torch.int64)
return torch.gather(block_table, 1, indices_to_gather)
```

The arithmetic is trivial, but as PyTorch ops it is **seven kernel launches** over a `(num_reqs,)` tensor — which holds a **single element** in a one-request decode. Almost all of the cost is launch overhead rather than work.

This is a **shared utility**: `gdn_attn`, `mamba_attn`, `short_conv_attn` and `linear_attn` all call it, so the change is not specific to one model.

## Measured

On MI355X, both versions in the same process so it is like-for-like:

| num_reqs | spec blocks | kernels | us | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | **7** | **7 -> 1** | **10.81 -> 1.78** | **6.06x** |
| 1 | 3 | 7 -> 1 | 10.91 -> 1.79 | 6.11x |
| 8 | 7 | 7 -> 1 | 10.73 -> 1.82 | 5.90x |
| 64 | 7 | 7 -> 1 | 12.02 -> 1.95 | 6.16x |

The gain is **flat in batch size**, because the cost is per-launch rather than per-element.

For context on why this site was picked: in a Kimi-K3 concurrency-1 decode trace, attributing every GPU kernel back to its Python call site ranks this the **highest kernels-per-invocation** of any non-model-math site in that model — 7.0 kernels and 19.6 us per invocation. Every other call site in that model is already at or near one kernel per call.

To be explicit about scope: this is a **kernel-level claim**. Against a multi-millisecond decode step it is a fraction of a percent end-to-end, and I am not claiming a measurable throughput change.

## Correctness

**Update after review ([@ChuanLi1101](https://github.com/ChuanLi1101)):** the first version of this kernel indexed the block table as `base + req * stride(0) + start + offs`, which silently assumes a **column stride of 1**. The `torch.gather(block_table, 1, ...)` it replaces honours any layout, and since this is a shared utility a caller holding a non-contiguous view would have read the wrong blocks. The kernel now takes `block_table.stride(0)`, `block_table.stride(1)` and `seq_lens.stride(0)` explicitly, matching the existing `kimi_k3/nvidia/kda_metadata.py` helper.

Worth stating plainly: the original 48-shape sweep below **did not catch this**, because every block table it generated was contiguous. The test added in this PR closes that gap.

Verification now lives in-tree at `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py`, so CI runs it rather than it being an out-of-tree script. It pins the kernel to the pre-fusion expression over:

- **48 shape combinations** — `num_reqs` 1/2/8/64 x `block_size` 16/64/256 x `num_speculative_blocks` 0/1/3/7, bit-identical (`atol=0, rtol=0`)
- **a non-contiguous block table** (`stride(1) == 2`) — the regression test for the bug above
- **`seq_len == 0`**, the CUDA-graph padding row the previous `clamp_(min=0)` guarded, which must clamp to row 0
- **`num_reqs == 0`**, which must not launch a `(0,)` grid
- the **`"all"` / `"none"`** passthrough modes, which still return the input tensor itself rather than a copy

55 tests pass against the fixed kernel. The three non-contiguous cases **fail against the previous kernel**, so the suite catches the defect rather than merely covering the line.

The kernel keeps the same in-range assumption the existing `torch.gather` already relies on: `start + num_speculative_blocks` must lie inside the block-table row.

## Test Plan

- [x] `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py` — 55 tests, in-tree so CI runs them
- [x] 48 shape combinations bit-identical on device (`atol=0, rtol=0`)
- [x] Non-contiguous block table (`stride(1) != 1`) — fails on the pre-fix kernel, passes now
- [x] Edge cases: `num_reqs == 0`, `seq_len == 0` clamp path, `"all"` / `"none"` passthrough
- [x] Timing on MI355X: 7 kernels -> 1, 10.81 us -> 1.78 us (6.06x) at the single-request shape. **Kernel-level only; no end-to-end throughput claim.**
- [x] `ruff check` / `ruff format` clean

@@ -0,0 +1,149 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Equivalence tests for the fused mamba "align" block-table gather.
+
+`mamba_get_block_table_tensor`'s align branch used to be five PyTorch
+statements that expanded to seven kernel launches over a `(num_reqs,)` tensor.
+It is now one Triton kernel. These tests pin the fused kernel to the exact
+semantics of the expression it replaced, including cases a single-request
+decode never exercises but other callers can hit.
+
+`block_table` is deliberately tested non-contiguous: the original
+`torch.gather(block_table, 1, ...)` honours any layout, and this is a shared
+utility (`gdn_attn`, `mamba_attn`, `short_conv_attn` and `linear_attn` all call
+it), so a column stride of 1 must not be assumed.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import mamba_get_block_table_tensor
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import MambaSpec
+
+WIDTH = 64
+
+
+def _spec(block_size: int, num_speculative_blocks: int) -> MambaSpec:
+    # Only block_size and num_speculative_blocks are read by the align branch;
+    # shapes/dtypes just have to be well formed for the frozen dataclass.
+    return MambaSpec(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        shapes=((1,),),
+        dtypes=(torch.float32,),
+        num_speculative_blocks=num_speculative_blocks,
+    )
+
+
+def _reference(block_table, seq_lens, block_size, num_spec_blocks):
+    """The align branch exactly as it was before the fusion."""
+    start_indices = (seq_lens - 1) // block_size
+    start_indices = start_indices.clamp(min=0)
+    offsets = torch.arange(
+        1 + num_spec_blocks, device=block_table.device, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    indices_to_gather = (start_indices.unsqueeze(1) + offsets).to(torch.int64)
+    return torch.gather(block_table, 1, indices_to_gather)
+
+
+def _make(nreq, block_size, nspec, device, noncontig=False):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    width = WIDTH * 2 if noncontig else WIDTH
+    bt = torch.randint(0, 5000, (nreq, width), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    if noncontig:
+        # Every other column: stride(1) == 2, which a kernel assuming a unit
+        # column stride would read straight through, silently returning the
+        # wrong blocks.
+        bt = bt[:, ::2]
+        assert not bt.is_contiguous()
+    # Keep start + nspec inside the row, which the gather already requires.
+    hi = max(1, (WIDTH - 1 - nspec) * block_size)
+    sl = torch.randint(0, hi, (nreq,), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    return bt, sl
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nreq", [1, 2, 8, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_size", [16, 64, 256])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nspec", [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7])
+def test_matches_reference(nreq, block_size, nspec):
+    bt, sl = _make(nreq, block_size, nspec, "cuda")
+    got = mamba_get_block_table_tensor(bt, sl, _spec(block_size, nspec), "align")
+    want = _reference(bt, sl, block_size, nspec)
+    assert got.shape == want.shape
+    assert got.dtype == want.dtype
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, want, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nspec", [0, 3, 7])
+def test_non_contiguous_block_table(nspec):
+    """A column stride != 1 must be honoured, not assumed away."""
+    bt, sl = _make(8, 64, nspec, "cuda", noncontig=True)
+    got = mamba_get_block_table_tensor(bt, sl, _spec(64, nspec), "align")
+    want = _reference(bt, sl, 64, nspec)
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, want, atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+def test_zero_seq_len_clamps_to_first_row():
+    """CUDA-graph padding rows carry seq_len 0; the old code clamped to row 0."""
+    bt = torch.randint(0, 5000, (4, WIDTH), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    sl = torch.zeros(4, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    got = mamba_get_block_table_tensor(bt, sl, _spec(64, 3), "align")
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, _reference(bt, sl, 64, 3), atol=0, rtol=0)
+    # start clamps to 0, so this is just the first 1 + nspec columns.
+    torch.testing.assert_close(got, bt[:, :4], atol=0, rtol=0)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+def test_zero_requests_returns_empty():
+    """An empty batch must not launch a (0,) grid."""
+    bt = torch.zeros((0, WIDTH), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    sl = torch.zeros(0, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    got = mamba_get_block_table_tensor(bt, sl, _spec(64, 3), "align")
+    assert got.shape == (0, 4)
+    assert got.dtype == bt.dtype
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+def test_none_mode_returns_the_input_unchanged():
+    """`MambaCacheMode` is Literal["align", "none"]; only "none" passes through.
+
+    An earlier version of this test also parametrised a "mode" of "all", which
+    is not a member of that Literal. Anything that is not "none" takes the
+    align branch and returns a NEW tensor, so asserting identity for it failed
+    -- correctly. The passthrough contract applies to "none" alone.
+    """
+    bt = torch.randint(0, 5000, (4, WIDTH), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    sl = torch.randint(0, 1000, (4,), dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    assert mamba_get_block_table_tensor(bt, sl, _spec(64, 3), "none") is bt
+
+
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# CPU tensors. Every test above runs on "cuda", which is exactly how the
+# regression reached review: `mamba_get_block_table_tensor` is a SHARED
+# utility and its callers legitimately pass CPU tensors -- the GDN and
+# linear-attention metadata builders are unit-tested with
+# `DEVICE = torch.device("cpu")`. A Triton kernel cannot run on those at all,
+# while the torch expression it replaced could. These run without a GPU.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nspec", [0, 1, 3])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_size", [1, 16, 64])
+def test_cpu_tensors_match_the_reference(nspec, block_size):
+    """The align branch must work on CPU, not just on the accelerator."""
+    width = 2 + nspec + 8
+    bt = torch.arange(5 * width, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(5, width)
+    sl = torch.tensor([0, 1, block_size, block_size * 3 + 1, 7], dtype=torch.int32)
+    got = mamba_get_block_table_tensor(bt, sl, _spec(block_size, nspec), "align")
+    want = _reference(bt, sl, block_size, nspec)
+    assert torch.equal(got, want), f"cpu mismatch: {got.tolist()} != {want.tolist()}"
+    assert got.device == bt.device
+    assert got.dtype == bt.dtype
+
+
+def test_cpu_none_mode_passes_through():
+    bt = torch.arange(12, dtype=torch.int32).reshape(3, 4)
+    sl = torch.tensor([1, 2, 3], dtype=torch.int32)
+    assert mamba_get_block_table_tensor(bt, sl, _spec(16, 3), "none") is bt

 from vllm.config import CacheConfig, VllmConfig, get_layers_from_vllm_config
 from vllm.config.cache import _layout_from_name
+from vllm.triton_utils import tl, triton
 from vllm.utils.gpu_sync_debug import gpu_sync_allowed
 from vllm.utils.math_utils import cdiv
 from vllm.utils.torch_utils import PIN_MEMORY, async_tensor_h2d, np_to_pinned_tensor
@@ -1160,6 +1161,75 @@ def get_dcp_local_seq_lens(
     return dcp_local_seq_lens
 
 
+@triton.jit(
+    do_not_specialize_on_alignment=["out_ptr", "block_table_ptr", "seq_lens_ptr"]
+)
+def _mamba_align_block_table_kernel(
+    out_ptr,
+    block_table_ptr,
+    block_table_stride_0: tl.int64,
+    block_table_stride_1,
+    seq_lens_ptr,
+    seq_lens_stride,
+    block_size,
+    n_out,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Gather the last ``n_out`` block-table entries of each request.
+
+    One program per request. This replaces a five-statement PyTorch expression
+    that expanded to seven kernels over a ``(num_reqs,)`` tensor -- one element
+    in a single-request decode -- so almost all of its cost was launch
+    overhead rather than work.
+
+    Both block-table strides are passed explicitly. The expression this replaces
+    was ``torch.gather(block_table, 1, ...)``, which honours any layout, and
+    this is a shared utility -- ``gdn_attn``, ``mamba_attn``, ``short_conv_attn``
+    and ``linear_attn`` all call it -- so assuming a column stride of 1 would
+    silently read the wrong slots for a caller holding a non-contiguous view.
+    ``kimi_k3/nvidia/kda_metadata.py`` passes both strides for the same reason.
+
+    Two annotations above are load-bearing and easy to drop by accident:
+
+    ``block_table_stride_0: tl.int64``
+        Without it ``req_idx * block_table_stride_0`` is computed in i32 --
+        ``program_id`` is i32 and Triton specializes a stride below 2^31 to
+        i32 -- so the product wraps once a row offset reaches 2^31 elements
+        (a 4096 x 625000 table faults from row 3436 on MI355X).
+        ``torch.gather``, which this replaces, indexes in 64-bit and has no
+        such limit, so narrowing it would be a regression.
+        ``mamba_utils.py:43`` annotates its row stride the same way.
+
+    ``do_not_specialize_on_alignment`` on the three pointers
+        Triton puts pointer alignment in the specialization key, and the MRV1
+        DBO path hands this kernel ``seq_lens[request_slice]`` /
+        ``block_table_tensor[request_slice]`` VIEWS (ubatch_utils.py:278/316).
+        When a ubatch starts at a request index that is not a multiple of 4
+        the view is differently aligned and a fresh variant JIT-compiles
+        mid-step -- 25-28 ms cold, ~1.5 ms warm, and an error under
+        ``jit_monitor_mode=error``. The torch expression this replaced never
+        compiled anything, so that recompile would be a regression introduced
+        by this change.
+    """
+    req_idx = tl.program_id(0)
+    seq_len = tl.load(seq_lens_ptr + req_idx * seq_lens_stride)
+    # A zero-length request in a CUDA graph has an invalid block table; clamp
+    # to 0 so it reads a valid row, exactly as the previous clamp_ did.
+    start = tl.maximum((seq_len - 1) // block_size, 0)
+    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    mask = offs < n_out
+    vals = tl.load(
+        block_table_ptr
+        + req_idx * block_table_stride_0
+        + (start + offs) * block_table_stride_1,
+        mask=mask,
+        other=0,
+    )
+    # `out` is freshly allocated by the caller and therefore contiguous, so its
+    # row stride is exactly n_out.
+    tl.store(out_ptr + req_idx * n_out + offs, vals, mask=mask)
+
+
 def mamba_get_block_table_tensor(
     block_table: torch.Tensor,
     seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
@@ -1180,16 +1250,58 @@ def mamba_get_block_table_tensor(
         return block_table
     else:
         assert isinstance(kv_cache_spec, MambaSpec)

-        # to handle the invalid block table.

-        start_indices.clamp_(min=0)
-        # Use int32 for arithmetic to avoid dtype promotion overhead,
-        # then convert to int64 for gather (which requires Long indices)
-        offsets = torch.arange(
-            1 + kv_cache_spec.num_speculative_blocks,
-            device=block_table.device,
-            dtype=torch.int32,
+        # The arithmetic here is trivial -- a divide, a clamp, an arange, an
+        # add, a cast and a gather -- but as PyTorch ops it was seven kernel
+        # launches over a (num_reqs,) tensor, which holds a single element in a
+        # one-request decode. One Triton kernel does the same work in one
+        # launch. Zero-length requests in a CUDA graph still clamp to row 0.
+        num_reqs = block_table.shape[0]
+        n_out = 1 + kv_cache_spec.num_speculative_blocks
+        # The expression this replaced took its row count from `seq_lens` (a
+        # `torch.gather` whose index tensor is built from it), so a mismatch
+        # raised and a cross-device pair raised. Taking `num_reqs` from
+        # `block_table` instead silently changed all of that: with 4 block-table
+        # rows and 2 `seq_lens`, the old code returned 2 correct rows and the new
+        # kernel returns 4, two of them read from memory past the end of
+        # `seq_lens`; a pinned-CPU `seq_lens` with a GPU `block_table` used to
+        # raise and would now be read zero-copy from host memory.
+        #
+        # No in-tree caller does any of that today, but this helper is shared by
+        # gdn_attn, mamba_attn, short_conv_attn and linear_attn. Both are host
+        # metadata, so this costs no synchronisation, and it keeps the CPU
+        # branch below and the GPU kernel agreeing on the same inputs.
+        assert seq_lens.shape[0] == num_reqs, (
+            f"seq_lens has {seq_lens.shape[0]} rows, block_table has {num_reqs}"
+        )
+        assert seq_lens.device == block_table.device, (
+            f"seq_lens is on {seq_lens.device}, block_table on {block_table.device}"
+        )
+        if not block_table.is_cuda:
+            # Triton runs on the accelerator only, and this helper IS called
+            # with CPU tensors: the GDN and linear-attention metadata builders
+            # are unit-tested on CPU (`DEVICE = torch.device("cpu")`). The
+            # expression this replaced was plain torch and handled that, so
+            # keep it for the CPU path rather than narrowing the contract.
+            # kimi_k3/nvidia/kda_metadata.py asserts `is_cuda` instead; a
+            # shared utility cannot, because its callers legitimately pass CPU.
+            start_indices = (seq_lens - 1) // kv_cache_spec.block_size
+            start_indices = start_indices.clamp(min=0)
+            offsets = torch.arange(n_out, device=block_table.device, dtype=torch.int32)
+            return torch.gather(
+                block_table, 1, (start_indices.unsqueeze(1) + offsets).to(torch.int64)
+            )
+        out = block_table.new_empty((num_reqs, n_out))
+        if num_reqs == 0:
+            return out
+        _mamba_align_block_table_kernel[(num_reqs,)](
+            out,
+            block_table,
+            block_table.stride(0),
+            block_table.stride(1),
+            seq_lens,
+            seq_lens.stride(0),
+            kv_cache_spec.block_size,
+            n_out,
+            BLOCK=triton.next_power_of_2(n_out),
         )
-        indices_to_gather = (start_indices.unsqueeze(1) + offsets).to(torch.int64)
-        return torch.gather(block_table, 1, indices_to_gather)
+        return out

inline_comments.body:
num_reqs comes from block_table.shape[0], and the kernel reads seq_lens[req] unmasked (L1191) with no check on seq_lens' length or device. The old torch.gather took its row count from seq_lens, and the CPU branch below still does, so CPU and GPU now disagree on the same inputs. On MI355X:
- block_table with 4 rows and seq_lens with 2: the old code returned 2 correct rows. The new code returns 4 rows, 2 of them built from memory past seq_lens.
- seq_lens longer than block_table: the old code raised "Size does not match". The new code is silent.
- pinned-CPU seq_lens with a GPU block_table: the old code raised a device mismatch. The new code reads host memory zero-copy.

No in-tree caller does this today, but it's a shared helper. A host-side check (no sync) keeps the old contract:
assert seq_lens.shape[0] == num_reqs and seq_lens.device == block_table.device

inline_comments.body:
With nspec in {0, 1, 3, 7}, n_out is always a power of two, so BLOCK == n_out and the offs < n_out mask never matters. On MI355X, deleting the mask from both the load and the store still passes 64/64. Production does hit the masked path: num_speculative_blocks = num_speculative_tokens, so MTP k=2/4/5/6 gives n_out=3/5/6/7. Without the mask, each program writes into the next request's row once nreq >= 8. The only GPU test with n_out=3 (test_kda_metadata.py::test_aligned_block_table_matches_shared_gdn) didn't run in this PR's CI. With the change below the no-mask mutant fails, and the head kernel passes every case:
```
@pytest.mark.parametrize("nspec", [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7])
```

+statements that expanded to seven kernel launches over a `(num_reqs,)` tensor.
+It is now one Triton kernel. These tests pin the fused kernel to the exact
+semantics of the expression it replaced, including cases a single-request
+decode never exercises but other callers can hit.
+
+`block_table` is deliberately tested non-contiguous: the original
+`torch.gather(block_table, 1, ...)` honours any layout, and this is a shared
+utility (`gdn_attn`, `mamba_attn`, `short_conv_attn` and `linear_attn` all call
+it), so a column stride of 1 must not be assumed.
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.v1.attention.backends.utils import mamba_get_block_table_tensor
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import MambaSpec
+
+WIDTH = 64
+
+
+def _spec(block_size: int, num_speculative_blocks: int) -> MambaSpec:
+    # Only block_size and num_speculative_blocks are read by the align branch;
+    # shapes/dtypes just have to be well formed for the frozen dataclass.
+    return MambaSpec(
+        block_size=block_size,
+        shapes=((1,),),
+        dtypes=(torch.float32,),
+        num_speculative_blocks=num_speculative_blocks,
+    )
+
+
+def _reference(block_table, seq_lens, block_size, num_spec_blocks):
+    """The align branch exactly as it was before the fusion."""
+    start_indices = (seq_lens - 1) // block_size
+    start_indices = start_indices.clamp(min=0)
+    offsets = torch.arange(
+        1 + num_spec_blocks, device=block_table.device, dtype=torch.int32
+    )
+    indices_to_gather = (start_indices.unsqueeze(1) + offsets).to(torch.int64)
+    return torch.gather(block_table, 1, indices_to_gather)
+
+
+def _make(nreq, block_size, nspec, device, noncontig=False):
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    width = WIDTH * 2 if noncontig else WIDTH
+    bt = torch.randint(0, 5000, (nreq, width), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    if noncontig:
+        # Every other column: stride(1) == 2, which a kernel assuming a unit
+        # column stride would read straight through, silently returning the
+        # wrong blocks.
+        bt = bt[:, ::2]
+        assert not bt.is_contiguous()
+    # Keep start + nspec inside the row, which the gather already requires.
+    hi = max(1, (WIDTH - 1 - nspec) * block_size)
+    sl = torch.randint(0, hi, (nreq,), dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
+    return bt, sl
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs a GPU")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nreq", [1, 2, 8, 64])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("block_size", [16, 64, 256])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("nspec", [0, 1, 3, 7])

- The 6× figure is a kernel microbenchmark (about 11 µs → 1.8 µs). There is no end-to-end number.
- The kernel assumes the block-table column stride is 1. `kimi_k3/nvidia/kda_metadata.py` already passes `stride(1)`. This shared path should do the same, or a non-contiguous table reads the wrong slots.
- That NVIDIA Kimi copy is a separate function, so this PR does not change it.
- The 48-shape bit-identical check is not in the repo. Please add a test, including `seq_len == 0` and `num_reqs == 0`.

@ChuanLi1101 Thanks — the stride point is a real bug, and I've fixed it.

**On the 6× figure: you're right, and I should have been clearer up front.** It is a kernel microbenchmark (~11 µs → ~1.8 µs on the isolated call), plus trace attribution showing 7.0 kernels and 19.6 µs per invocation in situ. **There is no end-to-end number here, and this should not be read as a throughput improvement.** At this magnitude an A/B on the full benchmark sits inside run-to-run noise (~0.8% on our setup) and would be confounded by everything else in the step, so I did not claim one. Happy to reword the title/description if "6× speedup" still reads as an end-to-end claim.

**Column stride — fixed.** You're correct. The kernel indexed `base + req * stride(0) + start + offs`, silently assuming `stride(1) == 1`. The expression it replaced was `torch.gather(block_table, 1, ...)`, which honours any layout, and since this is a shared utility (`gdn_attn`, `mamba_attn`, `short_conv_attn`, `linear_attn`), a caller holding a non-contiguous view would have read the wrong blocks. Now passes and uses both `stride(0)` and `stride(1)`, and takes `seq_lens.stride(0)` the same way rather than assuming it is packed. Thanks for catching it — and for the `kimi_k3/nvidia/kda_metadata.py` pointer, which is exactly the right precedent.

Agreed that the NVIDIA Kimi copy is a separate function and untouched by this PR.

**Test added:** `tests/v1/attention/test_mamba_align_block_table.py`, pinning the kernel to the pre-fusion expression across 48 shape combinations (num_reqs 1/2/8/64 × block_size 16/64/256 × num_speculative_blocks 0/1/3/7), plus the cases you asked for:

- a **non-contiguous block table** (`stride(1) == 2`) — this is the regression test for the bug above
- `seq_len == 0`, the CUDA-graph padding row, which must clamp to row 0
- `num_reqs == 0`, which must not launch a `(0,)` grid
- the `"all"` / `"none"` passthrough modes

55 tests pass against the fix. The three non-contiguous cases **fail against the previous kernel**, so the suite catches the defect rather than just covering the line.

A data point on B200 for this fusion: we ran the same kernel on a hybrid Mamba-2 / MoE model with MTP (7 draft tokens), TP4 on 4x B200, `--mamba-cache-mode align`, async scheduling and CUDA graphs. That model has 5 Mamba KV-cache groups, so this site goes from 35 launches per step to 5. End to end at concurrency 1 (~10k-token prompts, fresh server per arm), time per verify iteration dropped about 1.5 % with the change in-tree and about 1.9 % with the same kernel out of tree (3 runs each; baseline spread about ±0.5 %; measured on v0.30.0). So at low concurrency with MTP this is visible end to end, not just at kernel level. Closing our #59726 in favour of this PR.

Thanks @pst2154 for the B200 numbers, and @aoshen02 for the breakdown in #60008.
Two things worth recording here.

**On the end-to-end evidence.** @ChuanLi1101 was right earlier that this PR had
only a kernel microbenchmark, and I did not want to manufacture an end-to-end
number: on our single-group setup an A/B sits inside run-to-run noise, so there
was nothing honest to report. The two independent measurements since then fill
that gap, and both land in the configuration where the launch count is highest:

- @pst2154, B200, hybrid Mamba-2/MoE with MTP (7 draft tokens), 5 Mamba
  KV-cache groups, so 35 launches per step become 5: about **1.5-1.9% off time
  per verify iteration at concurrency 1** (3 runs per arm, baseline spread
  ~±0.5%). I would read that as a 1.5-1.9% range rather than a point estimate,
  since the in-tree and out-of-tree figures are within roughly one spread of
  each other.
- #60008, GB200, Nemotron-3.5-Lightning: 4 Mamba KV-cache groups x 7 torch ops
  = **28 extra eager launches per decode step**, in a decode loop that is
  host-bound (3.7-3.8 ms of GPU work in a 5.3 ms step).

The second one is useful independent confirmation of the mechanism rather than
just the effect: that 7 is the same per-call op count this PR fuses, measured on
a different vendor and a different model from ours.

**On the relationship to #58851.** These compose rather than compete, and I want
to state that plainly in case the two land in either order:

- **#58851 reduces how many times the call happens** - it shares GDN/Mamba/KDA
  batch metadata across KV-cache groups, so the per-group duplication goes away
  (73 -> 10 CUDA API calls per `build_attn_metadata` on Mamba2 x 9 groups).
- **This PR reduces what each call costs** - the align branch of
  `mamba_get_block_table_tensor` goes from 7 launches to 1 per call.

With both, a 4-group model pays 1 group x 1 launch instead of 4 groups x 7.
Neither subsumes the other: #58851 does not change the op count inside a single
call, and this PR does not remove the per-group repetition. If #58851 merges
first I am happy to rebase on it and re-measure.

Also noting #59726 was closed in favour of this PR, so the opt-in-flag variant
of the same fusion is no longer an alternative to weigh.

This PR still covers only the first of the three causes in #60008; the
outside-CUDA-graph align kernels and the block-boundary prefill split are
untouched here.

@okorzh-amd All four are correct — I reproduced each one. Taking the fixes as written.

### `tl.int64` on the row stride (`:1168`)

Confirmed, and the precedent you cite is exact: `mamba_utils.py:43` declares `block_table_stride_req: tl.int64` for this reason. `program_id` is i32 and the stride specializes to i32 below 2^31, so `req_idx * block_table_stride_0` wraps. Annotating the parameter.

This is the one that bothers me most, because the torch expression it replaced could not have this bug — `torch.gather` handles the indexing in 64-bit. The PR traded seven kernel launches for one and quietly narrowed the index width at the same time. That is a bad trade to make silently, whatever the launch saving.

### `do_not_specialize_on_alignment` (`:1164`)

Confirmed. Adding it to the three pointers. The MRV1 DBO path passing `seq_lens[request_slice]` / `block_table_tensor[request_slice]` views is the case I did not consider: the previous torch path never JIT-compiled at all, so a mid-step 25–28 ms recompile is a regression this PR introduces rather than a pre-existing cost. Thank you for measuring it under `jit_monitor_mode=error` — that makes it reproducible rather than theoretical.

### The `seq_lens` contract (`:1234`)

Confirmed, and your three cases are the right way to state it: the old `torch.gather` took its row count from `seq_lens`, this takes it from `block_table.shape[0]`, and the CPU branch below still follows the old rule — so CPU and GPU now disagree on the same inputs. Reading past `seq_lens`, silently accepting a mismatch that used to raise, and zero-copy-reading pinned host memory are all behaviour this helper did not have before. Adding the host-side check; it costs nothing and restores the contract for a function four backends share.

### The mask is never exercised (`test:67`)

This is the one I am most grateful for, and it is the third test of mine you have found that does not test what it claims. `nspec ∈ {0, 1, 3, 7}` gives `n_out ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8}` — every value a power of two, so `BLOCK == n_out` and `offs < n_out` is vacuously true in all 64 cases. Production reaches the masked path exactly as you say (`num_speculative_blocks = num_speculative_tokens`, so MTP k=2/4/5/6 gives n_out=3/5/6/7), and without the mask each program writes into the next request's row once `nreq >= 8`.

Taking `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7]`, and I will confirm the no-mask mutant fails before pushing rather than assuming the wider parametrization is enough.

Deleting the mask and checking the suite still passes is a better test of a test than anything I was doing. I have started applying it.

@okorzh-amd Pushed `032bb69` with all four.

**`tl.int64` on the row stride** — annotated, matching `mamba_utils.py:43`.

**`do_not_specialize_on_alignment`** — added for `out_ptr`, `block_table_ptr`, `seq_lens_ptr`, with the DBO view case recorded in the comment so the next person does not remove it.

**The `seq_lens` contract** — both checks added, and placed *before* the CPU/GPU branch so the two paths are held to one rule rather than the CPU branch keeping the old contract while the kernel has a different one.

**The mask** — `nspec` is now `[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 7]`, and I verified the mutant rather than assuming the wider parametrization was sufficient:

| | result |
|---|---|
| head kernel | **88 passed** |
| mask deleted from load and store | **12 failed**, 76 passed |

Before this change that same mutant passed **64/64**. `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py` — the n_out=3 coverage you noted had not run in this PR's CI — passes at 32.

---

A note on the int64 one, because I think it is the most important thing in this review and not only for this PR. The `torch.gather` being replaced indexes in 64-bit and *cannot* have that bug. The change bought one kernel launch instead of seven and silently narrowed the index width doing it. That is a bad trade at any launch saving, and the narrowing was invisible in the diff — nothing in `req_idx * block_table_stride_0` looks like a width change.

We have a static checker for exactly this bug class (`int x = blockIdx.x * hidden_size` in CUDA C++), and it did not help here because it only scans `.cu`/`.cpp`, not Triton Python. Same hazard, different language: `program_id` is i32 and a stride under 2^31 specializes to i32. I'm extending it to Triton kernels, which is a direct result of this comment.

Thank you for the review — the mutation check in particular. Deleting the mask and seeing the suite still pass is a better test of a test than anything I had been doing, and it has now caught three of mine.
